name: Proof of Estimate (poe-solana)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app (app/), static export, pointed at this devnet program. Only changes: base path, the IDL generated from the program source at the same commit (the committed app IDL is from a later program version), and /poll/?id= instead of /poll/[id] so it can be served statically.
learn: A forecasting poll stores the crowd's collective estimate on-chain: make_estimate takes a lower and upper bound, records the midpoint (lower+upper)/2 and the uncertainty (upper-lower)/100, and each poll lives at a PDA seeded by the global poll counter, so new polls get deterministic addresses.
source: programs/poe/src/contexts/create_poll.rs L21 (poll PDA = ["poll", num_polls le bytes])
steps: Clicked through the hosted app (test wallet 8WVm…): filled Create Poll and pressed Submit, which sent register_user + create_poll in one tx
Then moved the estimate slider on the new poll card and pressed Submit Estimate: make_estimate
register_user (mints 1000 POEKEN to the new user)
negative: register_user a second time for the same wallet is rejected (user PDA already in use, custom program error 0x0)
make_estimate with lower 70 > upper 30 is rejected (u16 underflow in upper-lower: program failed to complete)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the new poll card then showed 'Yes 60%, 1 forecaster, 1 estimate' read back from devnet. Earlier read-only check: /poll/?id=0 shows the poll detail and estimate history.
limits: Resolving polls and collecting points need the poll's resolver; not exercised in this run.

name: Picassol (on-chain pixel canvas)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 12 frontend (frontend/), static export on devnet. Only changes: base path, devnet RPC, this program ID, and a 0-SOL fee on recolouring. Its MongoDB points API (pages/api) needs the author's database and is not hosted, so the points counter stays at 0.
learn: Each pixel of a 200×200 canvas is its own account at a PDA seeded by ["pixel", x, y]: create_pixel validates 0–199 coordinates and initialises it, and update_pixel re-derives the same PDA from the stored x, y and bump, so anyone can recolour a pixel but nobody can forge its address.
source: Picassol/programs/picassol/src/lib.rs L122-L123 (update re-derives PDA with stored bump)
steps: Clicked an empty pixel on sol.college/dapps/picassol-hackathon/ with an injected test wallet: create_pixel
Same click on a local copy of the same build (pixel 33,173): create_pixel
update_pixel → rgb(20,241,149), read back from the account
negative: create_pixel at x=200 is rejected with InvalidXCoordinate
create_pixel on an existing pixel is rejected (account already initialised)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the canvas renders 200x200 cells, and clicking an empty cell sent create_pixel from the app's own code, on the live sol.college page as well.
limits: Points/leaderboard need the author's MongoDB backend and its /api/updateUserPoints route, which a static host can't serve (the app's POST gets 501; the pixel tx is unaffected).

name: TrustLock (dead man's switch)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app, static export, pointed at a program we built from switch/ at this commit and deployed fresh to devnet on 2026-11-10. Only changes: base path, output: 'export' and the program ID.
learn: A dead man's switch is an escrow PDA seeded by ["escrow", owner, seed] that holds SOL until a deadline: the owner must check in before the deadline to push it back, and once the clock passes it, claim lets the beneficiary drain and close the account. The program reads the Clock sysvar, so the rule is enforced on-chain, not by the app.
source: switch/programs/switch/src/lib.rs L10-L20 (initialize: deadline must be in the future)
lib.rs L30-L38 (checkin: only before the deadline)
lib.rs L40-L46 (claim: only after the deadline)
steps: UI: owner (test wallet 8WVm…) filled beneficiary + 0.1 SOL and pressed '15s Escrow for testing': initialize
UI: the same button's second tx, deposit 0.1 SOL
UI: owner pressed Cancel on that escrow: cancel, funds back
UI: beneficiary (test wallet AgrL…) opened the app and pressed Claim after the deadline: claim
deposit 0.02 SOL into the escrow PDA
claim after the deadline → beneficiary received 0.02118872 SOL, escrow closed
negative: initialize with a deadline in the past is rejected (InvalidDeadline)
claim before the deadline is rejected (DeadlineNotReached)
UI: Check In (+1 day) on an escrow whose 15s deadline had passed was rejected by the program: DeadlineExceeded (error 6002, lib.rs:33); no transaction landed
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the wallet connected from the Connect button, the dashboard listed the owner's escrows, and create, cancel and the beneficiary's claim all went through the app's own buttons.
limits: A successful Check In through the UI was not captured: the 15s/30s test escrows expire before the extension lands, and a date-picked escrow was not created. The beneficiary claims from their own wallet, because the app's IDL makes the beneficiary sign claim.

name: gree (mint an NFT with Metaplex metadata)
app_kind: The fork's own create-solana-dapp React app (web/). The author's initNft code was commented out, so the 'Run program' button did nothing; we re-enabled that same code (same accounts, seeds and metadata values) inside an async mutation and wired the button to it. Also: base path /dapps/gree/, hash routing for static hosting, and this devnet program ID. The diff is in tests/devnet/patches/gree.patch.
learn: One instruction mints a 1-of-1 NFT: init_nft mints 1 token to the signer's associated token account, then CPIs into Metaplex Token Metadata to create the metadata and master-edition accounts, both PDAs of the Metaplex program (seeds ["metadata", metadata program, mint] and the same plus "edition"), checked with seeds::program.
source: anchor/programs/gree/src/lib.rs L19-L80 (init_nft: mint_to, then create_metadata_accounts_v3 and the master-edition CPI)
lib.rs L107-L131 (metadata and master-edition PDAs with seeds::program)
steps: Clicked 'Run program' in the hosted app with an injected test wallet: NFT Gp7Ncuci… minted
init_nft from the flow script: supply 1, decimals 0, metadata owned by Metaplex with name GLC-20240317
negative: init_nft again with the same mint is rejected (mint account already in use, custom program error 0x0)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py): the app auto-connected, 'Run program' sent the transaction, and the page showed 'Minted NFT: Gp7Ncuci1Mb4FbuXjDtfLW9Penz6R5iLEhBYECYAkBEQ'.
limits: The metadata URI is the author's IPFS link; the Inventory page fetches it through Metaplex JS, which we did not check.

name: Web3 Splitter (split SPL-token payments by percentage)
app_kind: The fork's own Vue 3 + Vite app (src/), unchanged except: this devnet program ID in src/lib/useWorkspace.ts and its IDL, base path /dapps/web3-splitter/, and hash routing so the static host can serve /create, /action and /list.
learn: A vault PDA per (name, authority, mint) owns an associated token account; initialize checks that the percentages add up to 100, deposite moves tokens in and books each recipient's share, claim signs for the vault with PDA seeds. Running it on devnet also shows two real bugs worth studying: claim derives the signer seeds from the CLAIMER instead of the authority, and it transfers the whole vault balance instead of the claimer's share.
source: lib.rs L12-L60 (initialize: percentages must sum to 100 and match the recipients)
lib.rs L112-L150 (deposite: books each share, then a token transfer)
lib.rs L152-L200 (claim: seeds built from the claimer, transfers vault_balance)

UI: Actions page, 'Get it' loaded the vault, Deposite 25 tokens: vault token account 0 → 25
UI: Claim: 25 tokens back to the wallet (975 → 1000), vault total 0
Script: deposite 100 tokens, shares booked as [60, 40]
Script: update to 70/30 by the authority (booked shares stay [60, 40])
Script: claim by the authority received all 100 tokens, not its 60 (bug: transfers vault_balance); B's 40 is still booked but the vault is empty
Script: delete by the authority closes the vault account

claim by a wallet that is not a recipient: Unauthorized

claim by recipient B (not the authority): fails with 'Could not create program address with signer seeds' — the program signs with seeds built from the claimer, so only the authority can ever claim (bug in the fork)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py splitter, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the wallet connected from Select Wallet, and create, deposit and claim all went through the app's own buttons; the Actions page showed the vault 'sc-ui-0808', the mint and '100 % Claim' read from devnet.
limits: Because of the claim bug, a multi-recipient split cannot be paid out correctly: only the authority can claim, and it receives the whole balance. The app's QR deposit link points at the author's Cloud Run endpoint, which is not used here. The balance column shows NaN in the app.

name: OrbOracle (stake-weighted price oracle)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 15 static-export app, unchanged except for this devnet program ID (in the app's IDL and types) and base path /dapps/orboracle-solana/. Oracle pages are /o/?oracle=<address>.
learn: Anyone can create an oracle tied to a weight token. Holders lock tokens in the oracle's vault (they unlock after the deposit lock), submit prices, and the program keeps a time-decayed, token-weighted average; rewards come from SOL funded into the oracle account, and holders can vote to blacklist a submitter once votes reach the quorum.
source: lib.rs L20-L66 (initialize: validated params, PDA [oracle, authority, mint])
lib.rs L95-L145 (deposit_tokens: tokens locked into the vault)
lib.rs L212-L330 (submit_value: decayed weighted average and reward)

UI: Submit Value 123.45; the page then read back AGGREGATED 123.45 and LATEST 123.45 from devnet
Script: deposit 300 (A) and 100 (B) weight tokens; this is A's
Script: B submits 160.000000; aggregate becomes 152.500778 (weighted 3:1 with decay) and B is paid a reward from the pool
Script: B (100 of 400 tokens, above the 20% quorum) votes to blacklist A: A is blacklisted
Script: B withdraws 40 tokens after the lock
negative: initialize with an empty name: InvalidName

ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py orboracle, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): create, deposit and submit went through the app's own forms and buttons, and the oracle page showed the new value, the 50 unlocked tokens and the authority read from devnet.
limits: Whitelist votes, withdraw and vote-weight refresh were run from the script, not clicked. The explorer list is read with getProgramAccounts on the public RPC and can be slow.

name: sentient.send (winner-takes-all sentiment market)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js app as a static export, with this devnet program ID, the protocol authority set to our deployer, and base path /dapps/sentient-send/. Market pages are /market/?id=<address> instead of /market/<address>.
learn: A creator opens a market with 2–10 named sides and at least 1 SOL (2% fee, the rest split evenly across the sides). Anyone bets 0.01–1 SOL on a side until the end time. After that the side holding the most SOL wins, the market resolves on the first claim (or Resolve Market), and winners split the whole pool in proportion to their bets; the creator and the protocol authority split the fees.
source: lib.rs L34-L165 (create_market: side, amount and time checks; PDA [market, creator, question])
lib.rs L166-L264 (place_bet: min/max bet, side index, before end)
lib.rs L265-L319 (claim_winnings: resolve if needed, proportional payout, one claim)
lib.rs L320-L378 (claim_creator_fees: creator and protocol halves)

Script: create_market 1 SOL, Yes/No, ends in 75 s
Script: B bets 0.2 SOL on Yes

ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py sentient, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): create, bet, resolve and claim went through the app's own forms and buttons, and the market page read the result back from devnet.
limits: The question is a PDA seed, so questions over 32 bytes fail before any transaction is sent (the form allows 200 characters). The create form only accepts end dates from tomorrow, so the short market used for the claim was created by script. The fork's TypeScript does not type-check (MarketWithPrices drift), so the export is built with type errors ignored.

name: CipherVault (SOL multisig vault)
app_kind: The fork's own React + Vite app, unchanged except for the RPC (the fork points at a local validator), the IDL import (the committed IDL in app/src/anchor instead of target/, with this program's address) and base path /dapps/ciphervault/.
learn: A creator sets up a multisig with a list of owners and an approval threshold; its SOL sits in a program-owned vault PDA. Any owner can propose a SOL transfer (their own approval is recorded), other owners approve, and once approvals reach the threshold anyone can execute it, which moves lamports straight out of the vault.
source: create_multisig.rs (duplicate-owner check, initial deposit into the vault)
state/multisig.rs L18-L44 (PDAs [multisig, creator, name] and [vault, multisig])
create_transaction.rs (only owners can propose; proposer auto-approves)
approval_instruction.rs and fn_execute.rs (owner approval, threshold check, lamports moved from the vault)
steps: UI: test wallet m4Ac… filled New Multisig (2 of 2: m4Ac… and GpUq…, initial balance 1 SOL); the card then showed 2 of 2, PDA 8SpG83XG… and vault balance 1 SOL
UI: New Transaction, 0.02 SOL to E8xrtSuz… (the proposer's approval is recorded automatically)
UI: second test wallet GpUq… opened Transactions and clicked Approve
UI: same wallet clicked Execute; the table showed 2/2 and Executed, and the recipient's devnet balance read 0.02 SOL
Script: A proposes 0.05 SOL to recipient (A auto-approves)
negative: create with no initial amount (null): InstructionDidNotDeserialize, because #[instruction] declares amount as u64 while the handler takes Option<u64>
executing the same transaction a second time: Underflow. fn_execute never checks `executed`; the call was stopped only because the pending counter was already 0
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with two injected Wallet Standard test wallets (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py cipher / cipher-approve, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): create, propose, approve and execute all went through the app's own dialogs and buttons.
limits: The Initial Balance field is read with parseInt, so 0.5 SOL becomes 0; use whole SOL. The transaction table shows the amount as 0 SOL even though 0.02 SOL moved. The proposal-time NotEnoughSol check compares against the amount before it is set, so it never fires; only execute checks the vault. The token (SPL) option in the dialog is not implemented in the program. Lists are read with getProgramAccounts on the public RPC and can be slow.

name: Novengrid SOL staking (Colosseum)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 15 app (ui/) as a static export, with this devnet program ID and the hard-coded admin address set to our test wallet m4Ac… (the vault is a PDA of that admin). Admin page: /dapps/colosseum/admin/.
learn: An admin initialises a SOL vault (PDA of the admin) and funds it. Players stake SOL into it for a chosen duration and can't unstake before it ends; rewards accrue per second as staked × apy_rate × seconds / 31,536,000 and are paid out of the same vault.
source: instructions/sol_stake.rs (stake into the admin's vault PDA, player PDA [player, admin, player])
instructions/withdraw.rs (admin takes the whole vault balance)

UI: Admin Deposit 0.1 SOL into the reward vault
UI: main page, 0.05 SOL for 7 days, Stake SOL; the portfolio then showed 0.05 SOL / 7 days
Script: initialize apy_rate 100 (what the admin page sends)
Script: admin deposits 0.2 SOL of rewards
Script: B stakes 0.1 SOL for 20 s
Script: B calls config (no admin check; it creates and sets B's own vault, not the admin's)
Script: admin withdraws the whole vault balance (rent included)
negative: UI: UnStake right after staking: InvalidUnstakeTime (the app showed Unstaking Failed; nothing was sent)
initialize twice: Allocate: account Address { address: DhznFqUAMAQ283wLkGQfM4o7SsFwVUVWDafNHe4d7Dqf, base: None } already in use
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py colosseum, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): initialise, deposit, config, stake and claim went through the app's own buttons, and the early unstake was refused by the program.
limits: The shortest stake in the app is 7 days, so unstaking after the lock was run from the script (20 s stake). apy_rate is used as a plain multiplier: the admin page's default of 100 pays 100× the stake per year (the script's 0.1 SOL earned 6,024 lamports in about 12 s). Rewards, stakes and the admin's deposit share one vault, and withdraw sends its whole balance, rent included, to the admin, which closes the vault (seen in the script). The APY shown on the main page is a fixed '50%' label. config has no admin check, but it can only touch the caller's own vault.
